segments: The 17th cycle.
Arab Kings.
Ghazali {OCR?}, the great doctor of the Arabs,
and he was buried in Tarsus of Cilicia.
This man greatly reproached the Arabs in his teachings,
because they were concerned only with washings and the adornment of the body,
and from the cleansing of the heart,
from which sins spring forth, they were negligent.
And he strongly exhorted to asceticism and renunciation of the world.
And he used to cite many examples from the conduct of the desert fathers in that great writing of his,
and on this account we have mentioned him.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and twenty-four
(1424 of the Greeks) the wife of Qilij Arslan, the Sultan of Melitene, went forth,
and went and became the wife of Balak, the lord of the fortress of Bula.
For she said,
"From the Sultan I heard that at all times he used to praise you and say,
'There is none among all the Turkish emirs as wise and brave as Balak.'
And on this account I desire that I and my children may be protected under your name."
And thus she was protected.
And Balak was greatly exalted,
in that he became a husband, as they say, to the Sultan's wife.
And when that Khatun returned, she drove out the Atabeg,
and she and her son took up residence in the citadel of Melitene.
And another Turk also, who ruled over Hisn Ziyad and was oppressed by Balak,
sold the fortress to the Sultan of Melitene.
And after a little while, the son of Sultan Muhammad (Mahmud) of Khorasan arrived,
and took Hisn Ziyad from the Sultan of Melitene.
At this time, the people of Melitene showed great compassion,
and bought many captives of the people of the region of Hisn Ziyad and of the region of Arqa from the Turks,
and set them free.
And in the year five hundred and seven
(507) of the Arabs,
which is the year one thousand four hundred and twenty-five
(1425 {1426 in text?}) of the Greeks,
Tancred, the lord of Antioch, died,
and Roger reigned after him.
And Mawdud, with seven thousand horsemen who were with him, encountered Baldwin and Joscelin, with two thousand foot-soldiers and a small number of Frankish horsemen who were with them,
beside the Sea of Tiberias.
And the Franks were broken,
and one thousand and three hundred foot-soldiers among them were killed.
And then help arrived for the Franks from Tripoli with the son of Saint-Gilles,
and Roger, king of Antioch, also came with his army.
